experience.details: Conducted defense security research and technical analysis in government defense laboratory.
Hands-on vulnerability assessment and penetration testing across web and application targets.

projects.name: PhishSim AI
projects.subtitle: Autonomous Agentic Phishing Simulator & Security Awareness Platform
projects.red: I simulated targeted credential harvesting emails to test whether users catch suspicious senders and report them.
projects.blue: I enforced strict SPF and DMARC policies, configured passive lookalike domain monitoring, and gave employees an instant reporting button.
projects.description: Agentic email simulation engine with passive attack-surface auditing (PhishRecon) and dynamic executive risk briefings. The public demo runs in a sandbox mode without outbound email dispatch.
projects.limits: Public demo operates in sandbox mode without live email delivery. Full generation engine is private.

projects.name: AegisAgent
projects.subtitle: Action-Layer Security Gateway for Local AI Agents & Smart Hardware
projects.red: I sent prompt injections, role-spoofs, and encoded payloads to trick the AI agent into executing restricted tool actions.
projects.blue: I locked intent scopes before the model runs, validated tool arguments against strict schemas, and required human operator approval for dangerous actions.
projects.description: Security gateway interposing between local LLMs (Ollama) and device tools. Implements a 9-gate defense pipeline: injection detection, intent locking, RBAC, parameter guards, rate limiting, human approval, hardware bridging with physical Red Attack Blocked LED, output scanning, and SHA-256 audit chaining.
projects.limits: Parameter guard uses declarative keyword and allowlist checks rather than a full SQL AST parser. Intent lock can block valid paraphrased requests. Local network web and MQTT traffic is unencrypted.

projects.name: SentinelFlow
projects.subtitle: Explainable Hybrid Network Intrusion Detection System
projects.red: I replayed port scans, SYN floods, and ARP poisoning captures to evaluate how stealthy attacks slip past standard filters.
projects.blue: I paired deterministic heuristic rules with an unsupervised Isolation Forest baseline to flag traffic anomalies and map MITRE ATT&CK techniques.
projects.description: Hybrid NIDS designed for network security triage and offline PCAP analysis. Pairs deterministic heuristic detection (port scans, SYN floods, SSH brute force, ARP spoofing) with an unsupervised Isolation Forest baseline trained on benign traffic, providing ranked feature deviations and incident reports.
projects.limits: Designed for offline PCAP packet ingestion and time-windowed triage. Requires labeled baseline captures for Isolation Forest threshold calibration.

projects.name: SafeLine WAF Lab
projects.subtitle: Web Application Firewall & Vulnerability Testbed
projects.red: I mapped direct backend routes to vulnerable DVWA targets to verify application exposure before applying firewall protections.
projects.blue: I routed web traffic through SafeLine WAF with TLS termination to inspect incoming requests before they hit backend services.
projects.description: Cybersecurity home lab built with VirtualBox, Kali Linux, Ubuntu Server, DVWA, and SafeLine WAF. Completed setup: Kali and Ubuntu VMs, DVWA database, local DNS resolution, self-signed SSL certificate, SafeLine installation, and verified HTTPS reverse proxy routing. Attack and block tests have not yet been conducted.
projects.limits: Setup is in progress. The reverse proxy route is established, but attack tests and block verifications are pending. SafeLine has not yet blocked requests in this lab.

notes.title: Network Ports and Service Enumeration
notes.red: I probed target ports to map exposed daemons, banner versions, and unauthenticated network services.
notes.blue: I closed unneeded ports, bound sensitive services to localhost, and enforced strict firewall rules.
notes.summary: Deep dive into TCP/UDP ports, transport protocol mechanics, common service vulnerabilities (FTP, SSH, Telnet, HTTP, DNS, SMTP), and manual reconnaissance methods.

notes.title: OWASP Top 10 Web Application Vulnerabilities
notes.red: I manipulated parameters, bypassed access controls, and injected SQL and command payloads into web applications.
notes.blue: I enforced server-side authorization checks, parameterized database queries, and validated all user inputs.
notes.summary: Comprehensive analysis of the OWASP Top 10 security risks: Broken Access Control, Cryptographic Failures, SQL and Command Injection, SSRF, SSTI, and defensive mitigations.

notes.title: Hack The Box Starting Point: Core Vulnerability Concepts
notes.red: I surveyed target systems for default credentials, unauthenticated FTP, and unprotected SMB file shares.
notes.blue: I disabled plaintext protocols, enforced robust authentication, and restricted network share access.
notes.summary: Key operational lessons learned from HTB Starting Point machines Meow, Fawn, and Dancing: the dangers of default accounts, unauthenticated services, and open SMB shares.

notes.title: Hack The Box Starting Point: Tier 0 Walkthroughs
notes.red: I connected to misconfigured targets with default usernames and anonymous SMB shares to retrieve challenge flags.
notes.blue: I removed default credentials, required authentication for SMB shares, and restricted root logins.
notes.summary: Step-by-step technical walkthroughs for Hack The Box Tier 0 machines: Meow (Telnet enumeration), Fawn (anonymous FTP exploitation), and Dancing (SMB share enumeration).

notes.title: TryHackMe Machines: Basic Pentesting, RootMe & Kenobi
notes.red: I found hidden web endpoints, uploaded webshells through weak filters, and exploited misconfigured SUID binaries for root.
notes.blue: I validated uploaded file extensions, sanitized server paths, and stripped unnecessary SUID bits from host binaries.
notes.summary: Detailed analysis of three TryHackMe machine pathways: service enumeration on Basic Pentesting, webshell deployment on RootMe, and multi-service chaining with SUID privilege escalation on Kenobi.
